notable_absence.finding: No data-plane privilege/RBAC content on this page at all - the only access gate is the management-plane capella-role:project-owner prerequisite plus a support-plan/cloud-provider gate. Confirms the batch hypothesis that private-link pages are infrastructure/connectivity topics, not privilege-catalog topics.

cross_component_finding: This page introduces a THIRD wording variant for the already-flagged support-plan-gate inconsistency (docs-issues/... not yet filed under this exact name, but noted in requires-support-plan.json's registry note about 'Enterprise Support Plan' vs 'Enterprise Service Plan'). Here the gate is worded simply 'The Developer Pro or Enterprise plan' - dropping 'Support'/'Service' entirely. The sibling page add-azure-private-link.md (same batch, same feature family) instead says 'Enterprise Support Plan' verbatim. So even within one tightly-related 3-page feature family (AWS/Azure/GCP private-link), Couchbase's own docs cite the identical underlying commercial plan three different ways across the whole corpus now. Recurrence flagged, not treated as a new issue per batch instructions.
cross_product_finding: AWS PrivateLink is explicitly gated on cloud-provider identity (must be an AWS cluster) plus a management-plane role (Project Owner) plus a support-plan tier - a 3-axis gate with no server/ RBAC analog, consistent with the rest of this batch's security/ pages.
